Pentatonic

Make music with five notes.

A minor pentatonic uses A C D E G. Learn a small area first, then turn it into a phrase.

Try it on the fretboard ↗

Understand

The formula is 1 ♭3 4 5 ♭7. A is the root: the pink notes show where a phrase can feel settled. The diagram shows only notes inside the displayed fret window.

Standard high-G tuning: G C E A. The G string is higher than C and E; the string order is not a low-to-high pitch order.

Make the connection

A minor pentatonic has intervals 0, 3, 5, 7 and 10 semitones from A. C major pentatonic uses the same pitch classes but a different tonal centre. A shape is only a route through the notes: the root, the current chord and your phrasing determine what the listener hears.

Play it

Play A–C–D, pause, then E–G–A. Use the next A available on your strings. Repeat the phrase backwards without speeding up.

The phrase is A C D E | G E D A. On high-G ukulele it changes register; it is not an ascending scale. Keep the notes but invent a different rhythm on the second pass. End on A, then try ending on C and compare the effect.

Four lines, from top to bottom: A E C g. The lowercase g marks high G, not the lowest pitch. These examples use high-G GCEA; baritone DGBE needs different positions.

A worked example

Read left to right. Counts above mark the beats; numbers on the lines are frets; numbers below give the duration in beats. R = rest. Stacked fret numbers sound together. Start at 60 BPM.

Read the example as text
  1. Bar 1
    1. String 1 (A), Fret 0, A · 1 beats
    2. String 3 (C), Fret 0, C · 1 beats
    3. String 3 (C), Fret 2, D · 1 beats
    4. String 2 (E), Fret 0, E · 1 beats
  2. Bar 2
    1. String 2 (E), Fret 3, G · 1 beats
    2. String 2 (E), Fret 0, E · 1 beats
    3. String 3 (C), Fret 2, D · 1 beats
    4. String 1 (A), Fret 0, A · 1 beats

A mistake to avoid

Five notes do not guarantee a good fit over every chord. For example, a held C can rub against C♯ in A major. Listen to the accompaniment and favour a chord tone when you want a settled ending.

Listen and check

Leave a beat of silence between phrases. Finish first on C, then on A: listen to the different feeling of resolution. C major pentatonic shares these notes but has C as its centre.

Ready for the next step?

Play the phrase without looking, identify two A notes on the map, and create a second phrase with the same five notes and a different rhythm.
